ai.description: This slender snake reaches 30 cm. It is brown or grey above with a pale, often yellow-spotted belly. A distinctive dark nuchal collar and blunt, rounded tail tip identify the species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gongylosoma calamaria* is best distinguished by its smooth, glossy scales and a distinct, dark collar-like marking on the nape, which is absent in similar *Calamaria* species.
ai.habitat: *Gongylosoma calamaria* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found under leaf litter or logs at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Reed Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time burrowing through leaf litter or loose soil in search of small invertebrates like earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gongylosoma calamaria* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gongylosoma calamaria* is found in the Western Ghats and parts of peninsular India, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations from sea level to 1,500 meters.
